title: Kestrel and the Thorn
premise: Noor Nakamura has spent her life mapping the Hollow Valley, the one place the old gods cannot reach, believing its magic-dead borders keep her safe. When prayers begin piercing the veil and her maps start bleeding ink that shows places she's never drawn, Noor learns she is the last heir of the cartographer who broke the covenant between realms. To reforge it, she must leave the valley, bargain with a god who remembers being betrayed by her bloodline, and surrender the one memory that keeps her whole: her mother's face. In the end, Noor seals the new covenant at the cost of forgetting why she ever feared the gods—and chooses to map the world anew anyway.
about_author: Hazel Eriksen is a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing antique maps before turning to fiction full-time. She writes from a farmhouse in coastal Norway, where the fog often makes her feel like she lives on the edge of an unmapped realm herself.

chapters.title: The Ink That Bled
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. While surveying the valley's eastern ridge, Noor finds her finished maps redrawing themselves—rivers moving, roads appearing where none exist. A dying pilgrim stumbles into the valley, whispering that the old gods are answering prayers again and asking for 'the cartographer's daughter.' The emotional beat is quiet dread: the safety Noor built her life around is revealed as a cage someone else designed.

chapters.title: What the Valley Forgot
chapters.summary: Noor's POV, with interludes from the god Vessar's voice. Digging into the valley founders' records, Noor discovers her grandmother forged the covenant that banished magic—and shattered it deliberately, splitting it into three pieces hidden across realms. Vessar, half-awake and furious, offers her a bargain: restore the covenant or watch both realms starve of each other. The beat is reluctant resolve as Noor packs her satchel and steps past the border for the first time.

chapters.title: A Bargain in Broken Country
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Beyond the valley, magic is wild and hungry; Noor survives by mapping as she goes, learning that drawn boundaries can bind even gods. She recovers two covenant fragments—one from a drowned shrine, one bought with a lie she immediately regrets—before confronting Vessar, who demands the third piece: a living memory, freely given. The climax strikes when Noor realizes the price is her mother's face, the memory anchoring her identity. She gives it anyway.

chapters.title: The New Cartography
chapters.summary: Noor's POV, closing with Vessar's. Covenant reforged, Noor returns to a valley whose borders no longer hold—but neither do they imprison. Grieving a face she can no longer picture, she begins a new atlas: not of walls and wards, but of crossings between realms. Vessar, honoring the bargain, becomes her first correspondent. The resolution lands on bittersweet hope: justice was never the law's to give, and survival cost exactly what it promised—yet Noor draws forward anyway.
